component.name: AVD Feed + Connect Linux
component.summary: Connect to your Azure Virtual Desktop workspaces

description.p: AVD Feed + Connect is a native Linux client for Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) and Windows 365. Sign in with your work account and it lists the desktops and remote apps you are entitled to, just like the Microsoft Windows App on Windows and macOS — then launches them over RDP.
Features:

ul.li: In-app Microsoft Entra ID sign-in (interactive, so Conditional Access is honored)
Automatic workspace/resource discovery from the AVD feed
Workspace grid with the real per-resource icons
Camera and microphone redirection, and multi-monitor support
Bundles a hardened FreeRDP that survives audio-device changes mid-call

description.p: This is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

ul.li: Fixed copying text from the local machine into the remote session when running under Wayland (XWayland): pasted text now arrives correctly instead of silently failing. The 0.4.3 clipboard fix only covered native X11 sessions; this backports the later FreeRDP fix that also handles the XWayland clipboard format. Thanks to Ewerton Mattos for the fix.

New per-workspace "Client shortcuts" setting. The remote client reserves Right Shift + a key for its own shortcuts (disconnect, fullscreen, and so on), which can swallow those keys or, with a stuck modifier, end the session unexpectedly. You can now leave them as-is, force them on, or disable them so every key goes to the remote PC.

Security hardening: your sign-in token is now only ever sent to Microsoft hosts. Previously the server-supplied feed, connection, and icon addresses were trusted as-is, so a tampered feed response could have directed the token elsewhere; those addresses are now checked first.

The app now verifies the remote host's certificate by default, pinning it on first connect and refusing the session if it later changes — protection against a man-in-the-middle. If a host pool's certificates rotate and this blocks you from connecting, a new per-workspace "Server certificate" setting lets you turn verification off again.

Security hardening: the sign-in page shown when connecting is now restricted to the official Microsoft Entra login address, so a misbehaving remote host can't point that window (which carries your signed-in session) at any other site.

Fixed pasting from the local machine into the remote session: copied text now transfers correctly instead of silently failing (and no longer risks aborting the connection). Updated the bundled FreeRDP to the 3.32.1 release, which includes the clipboard fixes.

Fixed the resizable-window (/dynamic-resolution) option for host pools whose feed enables smart sizing: the session no longer exits at startup with "smart sizing and dynamic resolution are mutually exclusive", and it now reliably opens windowed instead of fullscreen.
Advanced flags that are typed incorrectly (for example an unterminated quote) now show a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

Support host pools that use username/password (NLA) sign-in instead of Microsoft Entra ID RDP authentication. The app now detects these and connects with an empty domain so the logon is accepted; FreeRDP prompts for your password at connect time.

New optional resizable window: add /dynamic-resolution to a workspace's Advanced flags and the session opens in a window whose remote resolution follows it as you resize, instead of always starting fullscreen (toggle fullscreen with Ctrl+Shift+Enter).

The Monitors setting is now honored: choosing Single monitor no longer opens the session spanning all your displays (it previously always used multi-monitor). All monitors and Automatic work as expected too.
The webcam indicator light now turns off when you stop the camera in a call, instead of staying lit until you disconnect (updated the bundled FreeRDP).

description.p: Updated to the GNOME 51 runtime for the latest system libraries and security updates. No change to features or how connections work.

A refreshed, modern look: tactile workspace tiles with clearer icons and status, a tidier header with an account menu, and a cleaner status bar. New Light / Dark / System appearance switch in the account menu (remembered between launches). No change to how connections work.
Sign-in and connections are smoother and more secure:

ul.li: Your sign-in is stored in the system login keyring (encrypted at rest) instead of a plaintext file; an existing token is migrated automatically.
Signing in again after your session expires is now usually a single click instead of re-entering your password, because the Microsoft sign-in is remembered between launches.
Connecting no longer opens a second sign-in window — the app obtains the connection token itself, silently, and only shows a window if your organization actually requires MFA at connect time.
Connections gain automatic reconnect, a keepalive that stops the gateway dropping idle sessions, and smoother, less-torn video.
A “Connecting…” animation now shows while the session is being established.

description.p: Make sign-in robust when you close it part-way (for example after picking the wrong account). The window's close button now always closes, reopening always starts a clean sign-in, and the page no longer comes up blank or spawns a stray window that can't be closed. Staying signed in is unaffected.

Fix sign-in problems introduced in 0.3.3 on some organizations: the window could hang on a blank "Trying to sign you in" page (Azure AD Seamless SSO, which needs Windows Kerberos and can't complete on Linux), or hit a "Keep your account secure" error. Sign-in returns to the reliable account-picker flow, which avoids both. Your saved workspaces and icons still appear instantly, and the workspace you double-clicked still connects on its own after you sign in.

Faster re-sign-in: a known account goes straight to its password/MFA page (no account picker, no "work or personal account?" question), and the workspace you double-clicked connects automatically afterwards. Workspace icons are now saved, so the grid looks complete on launch. When a Conditional Access sign-in-frequency policy refuses the silent token refresh, the status bar now says so.
Fix a blank sign-in window when connecting on some GPUs/drivers (WebKit DMABUF/GBM failure) by using software compositing for the connection's login page, which was blocking authentication.
Fix an instant disconnect on Wayland sessions: the sandbox now grants the real X11 socket, which the X11-forced connection needs (the previous fallback-x11 didn't provide it under Wayland).

New in-app Settings — right-click a workspace to set its display scale and single/multi-monitor (remembered per workspace), or set defaults from the menu. No terminal needed. Auto-detection remains the default.

The session now auto-adapts to your machine like the official clients: it detects your monitor count (single vs multi-monitor) and HiDPI scale and configures the remote to match. Override with AVD_SCALE, AVD_MULTIMON, or AVD_EXTRA_ARGS.
Fix a doubled/stacked desktop on some setups: connections default to a single fullscreen monitor again. Enable multi-monitor with AVD_EXTRA_ARGS="/multimon".

Connections now run over X11/XWayland to fix an immediate crash on native Wayland. Remote scaling follows the display (HiDPI 200% / standard 100%) instead of a fixed 200%; set AVD_SCALE or AVD_EXTRA_ARGS (e.g. "/multimon") to customize.
Rebuilt the UI on GTK4 with the modern WebKitGTK 6.0 engine. Fixes the embedded sign-in page freezing for organizations that use federated identity providers (ADFS, Okta, Ping, etc.).
Now builds FreeRDP from upstream master — the PulseAudio hot-unplug fixes that prevent mid-call freezes were merged upstream, so the fork is no longer needed.
Packaging: the downloadable bundle now self-updates via flatpak update (embeds the update URL + signing key).
Persistent session: reopening shows your workspaces immediately and refreshes the token in the background, like the Windows App. Sign-in is only required on first run or after an explicit sign out.
First release: feed discovery, in-app sign-in, workspace grid, and connect via a bundled hardened FreeRDP (camera/mic redirection).
